name: Ortur Laser Master 3 20W
tagline: Community-favorite open-frame diode : best LM3 value
tldr: The 20W LM3 is the configuration most buyers mean when they say 'Laser Master 3'. Strong engraving, light cutting, huge community : verify you are not accidentally ordering the 10W SKU.

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Often the best open-frame value for mixed engrave-and-cut hobby businesses
Large bed and mature Ortur community support at a mid-tier price
20W hits the sweet spot between S9 engraving speed and 40W cutting cost
LightBurn path is well documented for first-time Ortur owners
Strong pick when you need cuts but cannot justify enclosed or CO₂ pricing

editorialDepth.advantages: LM3 20W is the default recommendation in the buying guide for a reason: you get real cutting headroom on wood without CO₂ setup. Pair glasses, air assist, and window exhaust and you can run Etsy-style mixed orders credibly.
editorialDepth.limitations: Nothing here contains the beam or smoke for you. Cast acrylic and thick production plywood still push toward CO₂. Verify you are buying the 20W optical module, not a slower head in a similar-looking bundle.

cons: Verify the 20W SKU : same chassis, different modules
Open frame: kids, pets, and smoke are not contained
Clear cast acrylic and thick production cutting still favor CO₂, not diode power alone
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W module on Ortur Laser Master 3. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use air assist for cuts, lower scan speed for photo engraving. Multiple passes at moderate speed beat one aggressive pass. Check the flagship tier’s cut benchmark if you quote production times to customers.

accessories.note: 450 nm diode : verify OD with seller

mainObjective: Everyday engraving plus reliable light cutting on wood, leather, and dark acrylic
